key_points: Using Wearable Sensor Data Abstract: This research investigates the use of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in health monitoring through data obtained from wearable sensors.
As wearable technology becomes increasingly common, there is a significant opportunity to leverage RL for the development of advanced health management systems.

A review of current literature indicates that although RL has been effectively utilized for promoting behavior change and optimizing energy-efficient data transmission, there has been limited focus on real-time detection of health anomalies using straightforward and adaptable RL methods.
This project intends to address this gap by developing a lightweight Q-learning-based system aimed at identifying anomalies in wearable sensor data.

By prioritizing simplicity, interpretability, and suitability for resource-limited settings, this research aspires to offer a practical solution for RL-enhanced health monitoring, facilitating early intervention and enhancing patient outcomes.

Introduction: The rapid advancement of wearable technologies has transformed how individuals monitor their health, enabling continuous tracking of vital signs such as heart rate, physical activity, sleep patterns, and more.

key_points: Proposed Idea: In response to the identified gaps, this project proposes a Q-learning-based anomaly detection system for wearable health data.
The system will be trained to recognize deviations in physiological signals (e.g., heart rate, movement patterns) that may indicate stress, fatigue, or abnormal health conditions.
Unlike existing work that relies on complex deep learning models or focuses solely on behavioral nudging, this project emphasizes simplicity, adaptability, and real-time responsiveness.
The goal is to create a lightweight prototype suitable for limited-resource environments while retaining meaningful health insight.
